subject: phone in pocket
title: 89% of Students Felt Their Phone Buzz When It Never Did

scenes.text: Your phone just buzzed in your pocket. Except it didn't.
In a 2012 study of 290 college students, 89 percent had felt these phantom vibrations.
On average, about once every two weeks.
Hospital staff too: 68 percent in a 2010 survey felt their phone or pager buzz when nothing happened.
Your brain is so primed for the buzz that a twitch or brush of fabric gets read as a call.
The fix many found: turn vibrate off. Now check your pocket.

description:
Phantom vibrations are the feeling that your phone buzzed when it didn't.
In a 2012 study of 290 undergraduates (Drouin, Kaiser and Miller), 89% had experienced them, about once every two weeks on average. In a 2010 BMJ survey of hospital staff, 68% had; turning off vibrate stopped them for 75% of those who tried.
How often does it happen to you?
thumbnail_text: 89% FELT A BUZZ THAT NEVER CAME
first_comment: In the hospital survey, 13% felt phantom buzzes every single day. Did you check your pocket while watching this?
